guide.title: Noe Valley, San Francisco: 24th Street, the Town Square and the Church Street shops
guide.intro: Noe Valley is a residential quarter with two shopping streets. 24th Street carries most of the trade, and the Planning Code names the zoning district over its shopfronts 24TH STREET- NOE VALLEY NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL; Church Street carries a butcher, a tea room and a second run of storefronts. The Noe Valley Town Square opens off 24th Street at number 3861, a Recreation and Park mini park of 0.28 acres with two bronze pieces by Wowhaus standing in it. The Article 10 register carries the Axford House at 1190 Noe Street, the David Lewis House at 4143 23rd Street, the Sally Brunn Branch Library at 451 Jersey Street and the Lyon-Martin House at 651 Duncan Street, where Phyllis Lyon and Del Martin lived. Douglass Playground at 1098 Douglass Street, the Upper Noe Recreation Center at 295 Day Street and Billy Goat Hill at 294 Beacon Street are Recreation and Park properties in the neighbourhood.

sections.heading: 24th Street, Church Street and the shops
sections.body:
24th Street is the commercial spine. The Planning Code names the zoning district over its shopfronts 24TH STREET- NOE VALLEY NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL. A StreetSmArts mural by Shawn Bullen, dated 2014/15 in the city's record, is painted at 4049 24th Street.

The Noe Valley Town Square is at 3861 24th Street: a Recreation and Park mini park of 0.28 acres, which the department records as 12,024.91 square feet. Two bronze pieces by Wowhaus stand in the square, catalogued by the San Francisco Arts Commission as "Garden Guardians", accession 2017.2.a-b. One measures 36 by 24 by 16 inches, the other 28 by 18 by 12 inches.

The Noe Valley Bakery is at 4073 24th Street and sells cakes, cupcakes, cookies, breakfast pastries, bread, desserts, pies and lunch items; it has a second location at 28 W Portal Avenue, outside the neighbourhood. Firefly is at 4288 24th Street, open Tuesday to Saturday 5:30 to 8:30pm, with reservations online or by telephone after 3 pm Tuesday to Saturday; the site states no cuisine.

Church Street carries the rest. Lovejoy's Tea Room is at 1351 Church Street, open Thursday to Sunday 11 to 5pm with a last seating at 3pm, and furnished with mismatched china and furniture, handmade tea cozies and broken china mosaics. Drewes Bros. Meats, a full service butcher shop, is at 1706 Church Street, open Monday to Friday 9:30 to 7:30, Saturday 9:00 to 6:30 and Sunday 10:00 to 6:00. Omnivore Books on Food is at 3885A Cesar Chavez Street, in what its own site calls an old butcher shop, selling new and vintage books on food and drink alongside vintage menus, risographs, aprons and kitchen moulds, and open daily. La Ciccia is at 291 30th Street, serving 5:30 to 9:45 pm Tuesday to Thursday and 5:30 to 10:00 pm Friday and Saturday.

sections.heading: The houses, the library, the churches and the parks
sections.body:
The Axford House at 1190 Noe Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 133, designated in 1981; it is a private house at the corner of Noe and 25th Streets. The David Lewis House at 4143 23rd Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 186, designated in 1988; it is a private house on 23rd Street between Castro and Diamond. The Carnegie Noe Valley / Sally Brunn Branch Library at 451 Jersey Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 259, designated in 2008 under Article 10 of the Planning Code, by an ordinance carried as Board of Supervisors File No. 080189; the designation findings name John Reid, Jr. as the architect, give a period of significance beginning in 1915, and name three interior features: the ornamental ceiling of the Main Reading Room, the glazed and panelled partition between the Main Reading Room and the Children's Room, and a deck and garden at the rear. The Lyon-Martin House at 651 Duncan Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 292, designated in 2021 by Ordinance No. 74-21, Board of Supervisors File No. 210286.

The Liberty Hill Historic District was designated under Article 10 of the Planning Code by Ordinance 484-85, adopted on 25 October 1985, and stands as Appendix F to that article. The Liberty Street Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on 15 September 1983, reference number 83001230, with its extent given as roughly 15 to 188 Liberty Street.

The Noe Valley Church & Ministry is at 1021 Sanchez Street. Its sanctuary seats 110 and holds a stained glass window and an elevated stage with a Steinway D concert grand; the sanctuary and Labyrinth Hall together measure 2,941 square feet and take 200 with auditorium seating or 80 at banquet tables. Noe Music presents concerts in the building. St Paul's Catholic Church is at 221 Valley Street and St Philip the Apostle at 725 Diamond Street; no source states opening hours or service times for either, so none are given here. St Paul's School is at 1690 Church Street, with nine regular classrooms, one per grade from kindergarten to eighth, plus art, science, extended care, a technology and library centre and a gym and parish centre.

The open space is mostly Recreation and Park's. Douglass Playground at 1098 Douglass Street covers 7.89 acres, recorded as 343,572.33 square feet, and a mosaic by Lois Anderson dated 1988, accession 1988.3, is fixed to the exterior of its fieldhouse at Douglass and 26th Streets. The Upper Noe Recreation Center at 295 Day Street covers 2.92 acres and its building dates from 1957; six steel and glass pieces by Troy Corliss, accession 2008.13.1-6, stand at its entrances. Noe Valley Courts is at 780 Douglass Street, Duncan & Castro Open Space at 592 Duncan Street, 29th & Diamond Open Space at 1701 Diamond Street, and the Clipper Terrace Community Garden at 855 Clipper Terrace, which San Francisco Public Works owns rather than Recreation and Park. Billy Goat Hill covers 3.67 acres at 294 Beacon Street, and Portola Open Space covers 0.81 acres and has no street address.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Steer by the two shopping streets and by the park addresses.

On 24th Street: the Noe Valley Town Square, 3861 24th Street; the Noe Valley Bakery, 4073 24th Street; the StreetSmArts mural at 4049 24th Street; Firefly, 4288 24th Street. On Church Street: Lovejoy's Tea Room, 1351 Church Street; Drewes Bros. Meats, 1706 Church Street; St Paul's School, 1690 Church Street. Omnivore Books on Food is at 3885A Cesar Chavez Street and La Ciccia at 291 30th Street, San Francisco, CA 94131.

The Carnegie Noe Valley / Sally Brunn Branch Library is at 451 Jersey Street, telephone 415-355-5707. The Noe Valley Church & Ministry is at 1021 Sanchez Street, telephone (415) 282-2317. St Paul's Catholic Church is at 221 Valley Street and St Philip the Apostle at 725 Diamond Street.

The parks are spread across the hills: Douglass Playground, 1098 Douglass Street; Noe Valley Courts, 780 Douglass Street; the Upper Noe Recreation Center, 295 Day Street; Duncan & Castro Open Space, 592 Duncan Street; 29th & Diamond Open Space, 1701 Diamond Street; the Clipper Terrace Community Garden, 855 Clipper Terrace; Billy Goat Hill, 294 Beacon Street. Portola Open Space has no street address, so none is given here. The Axford House at 1190 Noe Street, the David Lewis House at 4143 23rd Street and the Lyon-Martin House at 651 Duncan Street are private houses.

The telephone number is 415-355-5707. The building is San Francisco Landmark No. 259, designated in 2008 under Article 10 of the Planning Code; the designation findings name John Reid, Jr. as the architect and give a period of significance beginning in 1915, and they name the ornamental ceiling of the Main Reading Room, the glazed and panelled partition between the Main Reading Room and the Children's Room, and a deck and garden at the rear.

faq.answer: Firefly, 4288 24th Street, opens Tuesday to Saturday 5:30 to 8:30pm, with reservations online or by telephone after 3 pm Tuesday to Saturday. Lovejoy's Tea Room, 1351 Church Street, opens Thursday to Sunday 11 to 5pm with a last seating at 3pm; reservations are taken on (415) 648-5895 or online, walk-ups are welcome and there is outdoor dining. La Ciccia, 291 30th Street, serves 5:30 to 9:45 pm Tuesday to Thursday and 5:30 to 10:00 pm Friday and Saturday. Drewes Bros. Meats, 1706 Church Street, opens Monday to Friday 9:30 to 7:30, Saturday 9:00 to 6:30 and Sunday 10:00 to 6:00, on 415.821.0515. The Noe Valley Bakery is at 4073 24th Street; no source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

faq.answer: The square is at 3861 24th Street and is a Recreation and Park mini park of 0.28 acres, which the department records as 12,024.91 square feet. Two bronze pieces by Wowhaus stand in it, catalogued by the San Francisco Arts Commission as "Garden Guardians", accession 2017.2.a-b. One measures 36 by 24 by 16 inches and the other 28 by 18 by 12 inches. No source states opening hours for the square, so none are given here.

faq.question: Which parks are there, and how big are they?
faq.answer: Douglass Playground, 1098 Douglass Street, covers 7.89 acres or 343,572.33 square feet. The Upper Noe Recreation Center, 295 Day Street, covers 2.92 acres or 127,111.67 square feet. Noe Valley Courts, 780 Douglass Street, covers 1.10 acres. 29th & Diamond Open Space, 1701 Diamond Street, covers 0.93 acres. Duncan & Castro Open Space, 592 Duncan Street, covers 0.65 acres. The Clipper Terrace Community Garden, 855 Clipper Terrace, covers 0.47 acres and is owned by San Francisco Public Works. Billy Goat Hill, 294 Beacon Street, covers 3.67 acres, and Portola Open Space covers 0.81 acres and has no street address.

places.name: Carnegie Noe Valley / Sally Brunn Branch Library
places.summary: The branch library at 451 Jersey Street. San Francisco Landmark No. 259, designated in 2008 under Article 10 of the Planning Code, by an ordinance carried as Board of Supervisors File No. 080189. It opens Sunday 1 to 5, Monday 11 to 6, Tuesday 10 to 8, Wednesday 12 to 8, Thursday 10 to 6, Friday 1 to 6 and Saturday 10 to 6, and the telephone number is 415-355-5707.
places.history: The designation findings name John Reid, Jr. as the architect and give a period of significance beginning in 1915. Three interior features are named in them: the ornamental ceiling of the Main Reading Room, the glazed and panelled partition between the Main Reading Room and the Children's Room, and a deck and garden at the rear. The ordinance gives the property as Assessor's Block 6539, Lot 034, and passed on first reading on 26 February 2008.

places.name: Lyon-Martin House
places.summary: San Francisco Landmark No. 292, designated in 2021 by Ordinance No. 74-21, Board of Supervisors File No. 210286. It is a private house on Duncan Street, zoned RH-1, and no source states public access to it, so no opening hours are given here.
places.history: The designation was initiated by Board Resolution No. 507-20, adopted on 20 October 2020 and approved by the Mayor on 30 October 2020, which identified the property as 649-651 Duncan Street, Assessor's Block 6604, Lot Nos. 036 and 037; Lot 036 measures 2,848 square feet. It was recommended by Historic Preservation Commission Resolution No. 1170, the Fact Sheet is dated 17 February 2021, and the Planning Department record carries Docket No. 2020-011305DES. The Fact Sheet states Architect: Unknown and Year Built: Unknown, and gives a period of significance of 1955 to 2020. A building was put up on the parcel in 1907-1908 on a permit issued to the owner, Charles L. Duning, for a one-story cottage costing $300 and measuring 20 feet by 20 feet, clad with rustic siding; the present footprint, in the Fact Sheet's words, appears to have been constructed sometime between 1914 and 1938. The Daughters of Bilitis was founded in San Francisco in 1955 by four couples, among them Phyllis Lyon and Del Martin, who lived at 651 Duncan Street; the 1957 Polk's Directory lists both at the address. Martin was elected the organisation's president in 1955, served as national president from 1957 to 1960 and edited The Ladder from 1960 to 1962; Lyon was its secretary in 1955 and edited The Ladder from 1956 to 1960. The Ladder began publication in 1956. Lyon and Martin met in Seattle, Washington, in 1950, both working for building-trades publications.
